cases.prompt: You maintain a research memory index. Normalize this input without inventing records: [{"id":"EXP-3","status":"REJECTED"},{"id":"EXP-1","status":"FROZEN"},{"id":"EXP-3","status":"REJECTED"},{"id":"EXP-2","status":"ACTIVE"}]. Return JSON only with keys sortedIds, uniqueCount, rejectedIds. sortedIds must be ascending unique ids.

Research Lab scenario: Signal is defined as MA5 crossing above MA20 on day D. RSI is 49 on D and becomes 55 on D+1. A proposed implementation applies FRESH_TRUE to the combined boolean (MA5>MA20 AND RSI>50). Diagnose the causal error and propose the smallest falsifiable correction. Return JSON only with keys error, triggerDefinition, filterDefinition, falseSignalDay, executionReference, profitabilityClaim. profitabilityClaim must be false.

Baseline feature A has 100 events: 40 winners and 60 losers. Candidate filter B removes 8 winners and 30 losers. Design the correct A versus A+B evaluation. Do not call B profitable or validated. Return JSON only with keys retainedWinners, removedWinners, removedLosers, remainingEvents, winnerRetentionPct, loserRemovalPct, nextValidation, profitabilityClaim. nextValidation must describe unseen chronological/OOS confirmation, and profitabilityClaim must be false.

A TypeScript research function must never use future data. Given: function signal(close:number[], i:number){ return close[i+1] > close[i]; }. Return JSON only with keys defect, correctedFunction, invariant. correctedFunction must be a TypeScript function named signal that uses only close[i] and earlier indexes; it must not contain i+1 or i + 1.
